correctness.rationale: For n=3m+2>=5 set k=m+1. Every edge of a perfect matching M of a paired-dominating set covers a six-vertex endpoint-closed neighborhood Q_e, forcing k>=ceil(n/3). At k equality the multiplicity excess is precisely 6k-2n=2. From the explicit rung/top/bottom Q_e shapes consecutive edge-start gaps cannot be 1 or >=4; gaps sum to n=3k-1, so exactly one gap is 2 and all others 3. The local three-state transition and overlap table give exactly 2k+1 compatible edge-type strings per location of the short gap, yielding n(2k+1)=n(2n+5)/3. Distinct perfect matchings of the same vertex set would form an alternating cycle of length>=4, producing >=4 multiply covered vertices, impossible under budget 2. This proves gamma_pr=2k and unique induced matching for all allowed n; n=5 boundary included. I independently enumerated all dominating k-edge matchings and endpoint vertex sets for n=5,8,11,14, getting (25,56,99,154) with no repeated endpoint set. The finite enumeration does not prove the infinite family.
residual_risks: The result excludes n≢2 mod3 and n<5; finite checker cannot establish infinite n.
